paragraphs: On Thursday, Teacher Kim's class had a science lesson. "Please open your textbook at page forty-seven," said Teacher Kim. The page was about bouncing balls. Everybody wanted to start the experiment. "Today we will do an experiment," she said. "Which ground makes a volleyball bounce highest: the floor, the grass, or the sand?" "I think the floor," said Leo. "I think the grass, because it is soft," said Mia.

First, Lily's team took a volleyball and a long ruler from the sports cupboard. They went to the school hall. "We must drop the ball from one meter every time," said May. Leo held the ruler next to the wall, and he looked carefully. Lily dropped the ball on the floor, and Leo watched the ruler. The ball bounced up to sixty centimeters. Mia recorded the number on a piece of paper.

Then they went out to the school field. Lily dropped the ball on the grass. This time, the ball bounced up to thirty centimeters. Mia wrote the second number. After that, they went to the sand box next to the field. Lily dropped the ball on the sand. The ball did not bounce well. It went up only ten centimeters.

Back in the classroom, the children made a table. First they wrote "floor", then "grass", and last "sand". They put the numbers next to the words. "Now tell me what you discovered," said Teacher Kim. "The floor is the best for a high bounce," said May. "The table shows it clearly." "I was wrong," said Mia, and she smiled. Leo smiled too, because he was right. "Soft ground is not good for a bouncing ball."

In the evening, Lily wrote the news for the class blog. She wrote about the experiment, and she put in the table. Then Mia sent a photo of the ball on the sand. Finally, Lily uploaded the post, and she called it "The Bouncing Volleyball". Teacher Kim read it and said, "Good work, everybody!" Leo wrote, "I was right, and that is the best news!"
